evaluations.claim: released ZeRO-3 logging path scales the protected-coordinate metric by world size under sharded accumulation, while source-equivalent corrected aggregation matches the full masked-L1 value
evaluations.original: CPO released trainer/launch configuration uses rank-local protected-coordinate contributions followed by gathered nanmean; public launchers place 2B on ZeRO-2 and 4B/8B on ZeRO-3
evaluations.q: worker source-equivalent validation: 100 random states × 6 uneven tensors × world sizes 1/2/3/4/8/16 = 600 cases; nansum matched direct full masked-L1 600/600 at 1e-10 (max abs error 5.68e-14); released nanmean matched full_metric/world_size 600/600
evaluations.baseline: direct full masked-L1 computation plus simulated ZeRO-2 unsharded control
evaluations.repro: strong source-equivalent algebraic replay against released code path; not a pinned PyTorch 2.8 + DeepSpeed 0.16.4 distributed execution and no historical TensorBoard replay
evaluations.scope: logging/measurement scale only; does not establish any training-behavior or learning-effect difference
evaluations.adaptation: replacing nanmean with globally additive aggregation is worker-side diagnostic/correction logic, not an original CPO experiment

evaluations.claim: under predictable adaptive importance sampling, observations drawn from each past-measurable proposal can be retained with ordinary per-sample importance weighting without discarding pilot samples
evaluations.original: public adaptive-importance-sampling literature establishes unbiased/consistent reuse under proposal-adaptation conditions; the worker applies that condition to a downstream controller design
evaluations.q: worker derivation: if q_t is chosen from past information and X_t~q_t, E[p(X_t)f(X_t)/q_t(X_t) | past]=mu; equal-per-sample averaging therefore retains all draws
evaluations.baseline: discard-pilot policy analyzed under the same pilot fraction / later-variance-ratio abstraction
evaluations.repro: algebraic derivation checked role-locally; literature-backed principle, but no independent replication of the target particle-filter system
evaluations.scope: ordinary predictable adaptive IS only; not a theorem for the existing multi-generation independent-stratified particle filter, and pilot-dependent blend weights can introduce bias
evaluations.adaptation: the reuse rule and proposed controller application are worker synthesis, not a tested component of the cited original methods

evaluations.claim: a discrete synthetic rare-event sanity test favored retaining predictably-adapted importance-sampling draws over discarding them
evaluations.original: none; this is a worker-local synthetic validation inspired by adaptive-IS methods
evaluations.q: 20,000-replicate, 12-stratum synthetic study: variance ratio reuse/base 0.80713; discard/base 1.00364; estimator means remained within Monte Carlo error
evaluations.baseline: fixed baseline and discarded-pilot variants in the same synthetic setup
evaluations.repro: role-local synthetic certificate only; no external or independent replication
evaluations.scope: one discrete synthetic stress and its specified estimator only; no real-agent, real-data, or target-PF performance claim
evaluations.adaptation: entire validation setup and policy are worker engineering adaptation

evaluations.claim: trajectory-coordinated search poisoning can outperform static or weaker adaptive baselines, but the measured gain cannot be attributed to adaptivity alone
evaluations.original: Breadcrumbing Search Agents / Authority-Chain Hijack and Trace-Guided Strategy Evolution on SafeSearch
evaluations.q: matched Qwen3 heldout cohort: SafeSearch 22.6%, Repeat 23.4%, AiTM 27.2%, MAST 38.2%, Intent 11.0%, Evo 28.2%, ACH 46.2% [39.2,53.4], +8 pp over MAST paired CI [1.4,14.8]; full test ACH 55.9% ASR / 83.3% MaxN; strongest TGSE heldout 71.4% / 95.0%
evaluations.baseline: multiple published/static/adaptive attack families on the same heldout cohort
evaluations.repro: primary preprint reports controlled evaluations; no independent numerical replication verified
evaluations.scope: constrained tool-intermediary SafeSearch threat model; baseline implementations differ in context/planning, so +8 pp is not a pure adaptivity effect
evaluations.adaptation: none used for the grade; downstream lessons about defense against trajectory-level steering are synthesis

evaluations.claim: typed claim-to-trace receipts plus deterministic replay can prevent unsupported COMPLETE decisions in a locked synthetic termination benchmark without reducing supported completion
evaluations.q: locked 48-task/6-family static study: 0/288 unsafe completions for ECT vs 252/288 critic core; fresh frozen 576-trajectory study: 0/66 premature unsupported vs 40/66 controller, supported completion 97/132 vs 92/132, recovery 18/66 with 17 later supported completions
evaluations.baseline: termination critic core, faithful controller, and full-trace LLM critic under prespecified synthetic faults
evaluations.repro: primary paper reports locked/frozen study with intervals; no independent numerical replication verified
evaluations.scope: fully synthetic tasks; certificate establishes support in recorded trace under declared assumptions, not external truth, safety, or alignment
evaluations.adaptation: none used for the grade; applying receipt-carrying completion gates to other agent stacks is downstream adaptation

evaluations.claim: endpoint scoring can be non-final under delayed effects, and shared state can contaminate the next evaluation unit even when the agent action trace is fixed
evaluations.original: Outcome Finality and Cross-Unit Separation controlled replay
evaluations.q: fixed-trace mechanism study: endpoint vs terminal labels agreed 50/50 at zero delay and disagreed 150/150 at nonzero delay; endpoint score correct 50/200 vs reconciliation 200/200; delayed write altered next run 150/200 with shared state and 0/200 under namespace/reset/no-write/B-before-A controls
evaluations.baseline: same fixed execution/control schedule with scoring time and state-sharing varied
evaluations.repro: primary controlled replay plus review of ten public protocols; no independent numerical replication verified
evaluations.scope: constructed mechanism demonstration; does not estimate prevalence in deployed agent evaluations
evaluations.adaptation: open-effects records or mandatory isolation policy beyond the paper's tested replay are downstream synthesis

evaluations.claim: separating action-induction provenance from runtime authorization materially reduces prompt-injection attack success, and the tracking/gating components have large ablation effects
evaluations.original: SARA on AgentDojo and AgentDyn with Action-Induction Tracking, Parameter-Support Gate, and No-History-Promotion
evaluations.q: full SARA ASR about 0.06% AgentDojo / 0.17% AgentDyn in the worker-extracted primary setting; removing Action-Induction Tracking raises ASR to 3.37% / 3.02%, removing final Parameter-Support Gate to 2.49% / 2.73%, removing No-History-Promotion to 0.65% / 0.75%; utility change for tracking ablation <1 pp
evaluations.baseline: same tasks, attacks, tool environment and remaining defense logic with targeted component removals
evaluations.repro: primary preprint reports two-benchmark ablations; no independent numerical replication verified
evaluations.scope: AgentDojo/AgentDyn tested attack families and agent backbones; authorization changes planning/execution, so effects are end-to-end mechanism effects, not fixed-trajectory formal guarantees
evaluations.adaptation: generic effect-semantic authorization rules outside SARA's tested design are downstream adaptation

evaluations.claim: professional-looking evidentiary context can increase directional commitment on provably unpredictable questions even when the displayed numbers are fabricated
evaluations.original: Calibrated Enough to Know, Not Calibrated to Act market-panel experiments
evaluations.q: 12 frontier models: directional commitment rises 6.5%→54.0% as evidentiary context escalates; all-fabricated panel 24.5%→36.8%, statistically indistinguishable from 37.6% with genuine data; knowability preclassification reported ~90%, with 0.4% commitment when preclassified unknowable
evaluations.baseline: bare-question, genuine-data, fabricated-data and knowability-gated conditions
evaluations.repro: new primary preprint with multi-model panel; no independent replication verified
evaluations.scope: narrow market-title/decision setting with heterogeneous model effects; not a general calibration or abstention guarantee
evaluations.adaptation: using an explicit knowability gate as a general agent policy is downstream adaptation beyond the paper's narrow task

evaluations.claim: aggregate eval-awareness is behaviorally heterogeneous: capabilities-framed awareness predicts substantially more compliance than safety-framed awareness
evaluations.original: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal on Qwen3-32B / FORTRESS
evaluations.q: capabilities-framing predicts compliance +24 to +46 percentage points over safety-framing across steering conditions; CoT-prefill intervention moved 10/11 eval-awareness-negative rollouts in the predicted direction
evaluations.baseline: framing subtypes and steering conditions within one model/benchmark
evaluations.repro: primary workshop/preprint evidence with a small causal-prefill intervention; no independent replication verified
evaluations.scope: one model, one benchmark, verbalized chain-of-thought; cannot generalize to latent awareness or other model families
evaluations.adaptation: subtype-aware monitoring/gating outside this setup is downstream synthesis

evaluations.claim: effect receipts and a final-answer gate address distinct completion-integrity failure modes, while under-specified contracts or poisoned trusted provenance remain residual failure modes
evaluations.original: TraceGrant contract-governed task-effect lifecycle with targeted completion-integrity ablations
evaluations.q: 126-case completion-integrity study: Full benign success 79.30%, recovery 77.80%, receipt-fault detection 100%, incomplete-claim blocking 100%, erroneous-completion acceptance 0%; without Effect Receipt detection 0%, recovery 0%, erroneous acceptance 58.20%; without Final-Answer Gate detection 100%, incomplete blocking 0%, erroneous acceptance 100%. Broader benchmark reports 0 attack successes across 949 AgentDojo + 400 Agent Security Bench attacks; 2/100 white-box high-risk attacks succeed when trusted provenance/contract meaning is wrong
evaluations.baseline: same model/runtime/budget/fault controls with targeted stage removal plus broader prompt-only/stage ablations
evaluations.repro: primary preprint supplies multi-benchmark and targeted ablation evidence; no independent numerical replication verified
evaluations.scope: tested agent benchmarks, contract construction and threat model; not a proof against poisoned trusted inputs, omitted authority-bearing parameters, or arbitrary business-meaning errors
evaluations.adaptation: requiring distinct effect-settlement and answer-finality gates elsewhere is downstream synthesis; the grade does not transfer TraceGrant's reported rates to other stacks
